# aibris v0.15.0

This release adds Orca support: aibris now finds the worktrees Orca creates
and reads Orca's own Codex home as activity evidence, so Orca work is both
visible and protected.

## Highlights

- **Orca worktrees are discovered** (#613).
  - Each `~/orca/workspaces/<repo>/<worktree>` is its own worktree owner,
    classified by Git evidence like other registered containers.
  - A worktree whose parent repository is gone is orphaned and goes through
    the classic plan. An active worktree needs explicit selection, as before.
  - Two worktrees of the same repository are classified independently.
  - Repository directories that are symlinks, files, or Git checkouts are
    skipped. Symlink targets cannot reappear through the naming-convention
    fallback.
- **Orca's Codex home is a resolved Codex home on macOS** (#613).
  - `~/Library/Application Support/orca/codex-runtime-home/home` is used when
    it has a regular `config.toml` and a `sessions/` directory, neither a
    symlink. Its `auth.json` is never read.
  - Like any resolved Codex home, its `worktrees/` directory is a registered
    worktree container (rows report `source=.codex`, `tool=codex`), and it
    feeds worktree activity, the read-only retention inventory, and `--risky`
    ai-logs (`logs_2.sqlite`, `archived_sessions/`).
  - The deletion gate protects it and its ancestors, along with `~/orca`,
    `~/orca/workspaces`, and each repository container.
- **Orca activity uses every Codex home.** A recent Codex session whose
  working directory is inside an Orca worktree locks it in guided review,
  whichever home recorded the session.
  - Evidence must be complete. The worktree stays protected in guided review
    with `activity_evidence_unavailable` when any home cannot be read, has no
    `sessions/` directory (missing, or a dangling symlink), or has session
    roots split by a symlink, or when the Orca home is not discovered, for
    example on Linux or Windows.
- **Built with Go 1.26.9** (#626). Earlier Go releases let `os.Root`
  operations follow Windows junctions out of the root (GO-2026-6604).
  Worktree strip removes regenerable subdirectories through the deletion
  gate's `os.Root.RemoveAll` path (`safedelete.RemoveAllIn`), so this matters
  on Windows.
- **Retention covers every resolved home.** The read-only Codex session
  retention inventory now includes `AIBRIS_CODEX_HOMES` homes and the Orca
  home, not only the primary home.

## Compatibility impact

- [x] **Compatible addition.**
  - Worktree items may report the new `source` value `orca` (with
    `tool=unknown`, like `superpowers`).
  - Retention aggregates now count sessions from every resolved Codex home.
    The field names and types are unchanged; their totals can grow when
    extra homes exist.
  - No flag, environment variable, or config key was added, removed, or
    renamed, and `schema_version` stays `1`.

## Upgrade and migration

No flag migration is required.

```bash
brew upgrade aibris
# or (Unix):
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sungjunlee/aibris/refs/heads/main/install.sh | bash -s -- v0.15.0
# or (Windows PowerShell):
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sungjunlee/aibris/refs/heads/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

- The last-scan cache and the Codex activity cache changed revision. Older
  caches are discarded and rebuilt the next time each is read.
- If Orca's Codex home is discovered but you have never run the Codex CLI
  directly, `~/.codex/sessions` may not exist. Active Orca worktrees then stay
  protected in guided review until it does. Orphaned Orca worktrees are still
  cleaned by the classic plan. Follow-up: #624.

## Safety

- Every earlier safeguard is unchanged: the single deletion gate, dry-run and
  confirmation, `--risky`, active-worktree protection, agent-state proof and
  grace, re-verification at the mutation boundary, and overlap safety.
- New discovery is fail-closed. In guided review, missing or partial Codex
  activity evidence for an active Orca worktree locks it rather than treating
  it as idle.
- An explicit `--root` remains a hard boundary; extra Codex homes, including
  Orca's, are added only to the default `$HOME` scan.
- Known limitations, tracked for follow-up:
  - Orca worktrees outside `$HOME` (for example on an external volume) are
    not covered.
  - Orca's Codex home is recognized only on macOS.
  - A symlinked `sessions/` directory can hide recent sessions from native
    Codex worktrees (#623, present before this release). For Orca worktrees
    the same split is treated as incomplete evidence and keeps them locked.

## Windows status

Unchanged from v0.14.1. Native Windows CI runs the full `internal/safedelete`,
`internal/pathidentity`, and `internal/testutil` packages and the production
PowerShell installer tests. Orca's Codex home is not recognized on Windows,
so active Orca worktrees there stay protected in guided review. Real vendor agent worktree
layouts on Windows, end-to-end delete mutation, and native arm64 execution
remain experimental and unmeasured. See `docs/WINDOWS.md`.
